newsitem.title: USA: Abraham--service industries buoyed U.S. March jobs.
newsitem.headline: Abraham--service industries buoyed U.S. March jobs.

text.p: Katharine Abraham, commissioner of the Bureau of Labor Statistics, said Friday that nearly two thirds of job growth in March occurred in the service industry, where employment rose by 111,000.

She said in a statement that construction employment levels, which fell 27,000 in March, reflected "unusual winter weather patterns and the statistical difficulties inherent in adjusting for these fluctuating seasonal conditions."
"A longer-term view suggests that underlying job growth in the (construction) industry has been quite strong," she added.
Abraham said that since last October the average monthly employment gain in the construction industry has been 30,000, somewhat above the monthly average in the prior 12 months.
She also noted that over the past year, average hourly earnings have increased by four percent, the largest such increase since the 12 months ended June 1990.
"The pace of earnings growth has continued to drift upward for several years now," Abraham said.
The ratio of those employed to the overall population rose to a record 63.8 percent in March, versus 63.5 in February.
